This first application has been filed by applicants under Section 483 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 for grant of bail in connection with Crime No. 782/2024 registered at Police Station-Vijay Nagar, District Indore, (M.P.) for offence punishable under Sections 376(2)(n), 294,
323 and 506 of IPC.
The applicant is in judicial custody since 16.11.2024.

As per the case of prosecution, the prosecutrix aged around 23 years reported to P.S. Vijay Nagar,
Indore(Urban) on 15.11.2024 that she got friendly with Bilal Azam in year 2022.

On 15.08.2022,
Bilal came to her rented room and proposed to marry her.
When she declined, Bilal touched her with bad intention.
Despite her resistance, Bilal forcefully had sexual relations with her and threatened to make her videos viral.
Thereafter, on multiple occasions, Bilal had forceful relations with her under threat of NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:9624 2 MCRC-2344-2025 making her videos viral.
In September, 2022, she shifted to Bangalore.
She returned to Indore in 2023 and started residing in a rented flat.
Bilal again started visiting her flat.
When she refused communication with him, Bilal abused her in filthy language and threatened to kill her and make her videos viral.
On 14.11.2024, Bilal called her on phone.

When she informed her friend Anilesh,
Bilal also called him.
Therefore, she came to report with Anilesh.

sentences.text: Bilal was apprehended on 16.11.2024.
He is in custody ever since.
The statement of prosecutrix were recorded u/S 180 and 183 of BNSS, 2023.
Prosecutrix further stated that Bilal has blackmailed and taken Rs. 2,20,000/- from her.
Bilal came to her flat and smashed the mirror and other house hold articles.
Relevant seizures were made.
On completion of investigation, final report was submitted.
Learned Counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is falsely implicated in this matter .
It is a case of consensual relationship between two well educated adults.
When the relationship turned sour and applicant took objection to friendship of prosecutrix with other person, false allegation of rape and extortion are made against the applicant.
No offence, as alleged, is committed by the applicant.
Prosecutrix(PW-1) had already been examined before trial Court.
There is no likelihood of influencing the remaining evidence by the applicant.
Applicant is aged 26 years.
He is in a private job.
The trial would take time to complete.
Therefore, applicant may be extended the benefit of bail.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:9624 3 MCRC-2344-2025

Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent/State ably assisted by learned counsel for the objector opposes the bail application on the ground of gravity of alleged offence and submits that the applicant had sexually assaulted and manipulated the prosecutrix.
Feeling aggrieved by constant harassment and exploitation by the applicant, prosecutrix finally lodged the report against him.
Therefore, applicant does not deserve to be released on bail.
However, after going through the case diary, he fairly states that no criminal antecedent is reported against the applicant.
Heard the arguments, perused the grounds for grant of bail stated in the application and the case diary.
Allegedly, the applicant committed rape on the prosecutrix on 15.08.2022 and thereafter, on multiple occasions in the year 2022.
When the prosecutrix returned to Indore, applicant again approached her.
Applicant manhandled, abused and threatened her.
The FIR is delayed.
The veracity of prosecution will be determined after evidence in trial.
As informed, applicant is aged 26 years.
He is in a private job.
Considering these aspects, there appears to be no possibility of fleeing from justice.

In absence of criminal antecedents, considering the socio- economic status of the applicant, there appears to be no likelihood of tampering with remaining evidence or influencing the remaining witnesses by the applicant or repeating the offence.
The trial would take time to conclude.
There appears to be no compelling reason to continue incarceration of the young applicant.
However, the observations, herein-above, are recorded for present application only.

Considering the rival contentions and overall circumstances of the case, in NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:9624 4 MCRC-2344-2025 the light of aforesaid facts, but without commenting on the merits, this Court is inclined to release the applicant on bail.
Thus, present application is allowed.

Accordingly, it is directed that applicant- Bilal Azam shall be released on bail in connection with the crime as stated in para-1 of this order, upon furnishing personal bond and surety bond of amount, as may be considered appropriate by the Trial Court/Committal Court for compliance with conditions,

2023, to secure presence of the applicant for the trial.
This order shall be effective till the end of trial.
